subject: Clarifying purchase lane: Marketplace (GCP) vs Private Offer — invoice routing / SKUs / co-sell credits
messages:

Subject: Purchase route question: GCP Marketplace vs Private Offer

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we move toward procurement: our finance team is trying to pick the cleanest path for invoicing and tax treatment. Integratek prefers vendor invoices we can route into our AP system (PO-based). Can you confirm the differences between buying Redwood via GCP Marketplace (public listing / Marketplace SKUs) versus a Private Offer / direct invoice? Specifically:

- Which path results in Integratek receiving a Redwood invoice vs a GCP reseller invoice?
- Are there delays to receiving co-sell or reseller credits if we buy through the marketplace?
- Do private offers allow custom SKUs or billing names (for POs)?

We also have a draft SOW attached that references Redwood as vendor; wondering if that needs adjustments depending on lane.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Desai
Head of Procurement, Integratek

Subject: Re: Purchase route question: GCP Marketplace vs Private Offer

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then detail below:

- Marketplace (GCP): invoice typically issued by GCP (or reseller) to Integratek; Redwood shows as seller-of-record in product metadata but invoice routing is via Google.
- Private Offer / Direct: Redwood (or Redwood's chosen billing entity) can issue the invoice directly to Integratek; private offers can support custom billing/legal names and PO flow.
- Co-sell credits: timing varies; buying on marketplace can delay partner credit recognition by a billing cycle or two. Private offers let us expedite co-sell recording and assign credits more deterministically.

I copied Vanessa (sales ops) for details on SKUs / PO-friendly fields and Karthik for co-sell mechanics. Below are the specifics so you can share with your AP team.

Marketplace (GCP public listing)
- Billing: GCP issues the invoice (Integratek pays Google). Redwood receives settlement from GCP per their payout schedule.
- Invoice metadata: limited custom fields; PO numbers are supported in some cases but invoice will show Google as biller.
- SKUs: marketplace SKU set is fixed; we cannot inject custom SKU strings.
- Co-sell / credits: partner credit recording can be delayed; attribution is tied to Marketplace order IDs which we reconcile after settlement.

Private Offer (GCP private pricing / direct contract)
- Billing: Redwood can be set as seller-of-record / issuer of invoice if we elect to route directly; integrates cleanly with PO-based AP workflows.
- SKUs / legal name: we can include Integratek-specific bill-to information and map a custom SKU on the PO side.
- Co-sell / credits: co-sell recording can be performed at time of contract execution and tracked against the deal id; typically faster for crediting and reporting.

I'll follow up with Vanessa to send a one-page comparison and example invoice metadata.

Best,
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Invoice examples and SKU notes (Marketplace vs Private Offer)

Maya / Team —

Attached is a short spreadsheet with two example invoice headers and a mapping of where the PO and tax fields show up in each flow (Redwood_marketplace_vs_private-pricing-matrix.xlsx). Highlights: 

- If Integratek needs Redwood as the legal invoicing entity on the face of the invoice (for your AP rules), choose Private Offer. We can put the exact legal name + remit-to + PO number in the invoice.
- Marketplace invoices will reference Google as the billing party; your AP team will need to accept a reseller invoice. If your system requires vendor VAT IDs to match the remit name, this can cause reconciliation friction.
- Private Offers also allow us to issue a Redwood-branded invoice and include line-item SKUs that match your internal chart-of-accounts.

Practical note: Private Offers add a small administrative lead time (we generate a private pricing agreement and publish a private listing) but the procurement path is usually faster from an AP acceptance standpoint.

Attachment: Redwood_marketplace_vs_private-pricing-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Hi Maya — quick answers from the co-sell/channel side:

1) Tax remittance: when GCP invoices, Google typically remits VAT/sales tax as the merchant-of-record depending on the jurisdiction; however, tax liability can depend on your local rules and the marketplace agreement. If you have a specific tax counsel question we can loop in our tax team.

2) Corrected invoices: yes, with a Private Offer Redwood can issue adjusted/corrected invoices that include your PO number and any required tax fields. That path is the cleanest if your AP needs Redwood as the vendor on paper.

3) Co-sell credits timing: marketplace orders are trackable but partner crediting is often reconciled on Google’s payout cadence; that can introduce a delay of 30–90 days before credits are visible. For customers where co-sell timing matters (rebates, channel programs), we recommend Private Offer so we can assign and document credits upfront and expedite internal approvals.

Operational suggestion: start with a Private Offer for the first committed period (or pilot) so your AP has clean invoices and co-sell credits are recorded quickly; later we can discuss public listing for self-serve expansion if desired.

If 10:00am PT 8/5 works, I can join the call and we’ll bring one of our finance leads if you want to cover tax specifics.

— Karthik
